Slot 0 is 6 o'clock; slot numbers increase clockwise. The document stores that many recent colors. Fill, Stroke, and text editors keep showing the first 6 only. A color seen for the first time fills the next empty slot. At 24, the oldest color is dropped, survivors pack back against 6 o'clock, and the new color takes the next slot. Using a color already on the ring moves it to 6 o'clock and refreshes its age. The wheel opens translated so the current foreground sits under the pointer. Dragging inside the disk changes saturation and value; the disk's rim reaches every corner of the square, so pure white and pure black sit on it, and a small snap there returns exactly #FFFFFF and #000000. The gap between disk and ring is dead: it keeps the last value and never samples (user, 27 September 2026: "gap should not have hit detction for either side"). Dragging in the hue ring changes hue. Past the ring the hold keeps its color until the pointer leaves the wheel's outer disc; only then does it sample the screen. Entering a dot's 10 px hit radius adopts that color and moves the pointer to the center of that painted dot, each time a dot is newly entered. The wheel stays where it opened. The ring reshuffles on release. Readout type is window chrome. The wheel and HUD numbers stay in screen px. The width circle stays world times zoom.

D10.behavior: Idle Brush and the size HUD paint a filled tip in the foreground color. The fill is opaque from the center out to (1 - softness) of the radius, then fades to clear at the rim. A thin white ring marks the full diameter. While Alt is held the eyedropper cursor replaces it: the foreground swatch is a ring, so the pixel under the hotspot, which the sample reads, still shows the canvas. The tip circle is the cursor for Brush and Eraser: the OS arrow hides under it over the board (stated 2026-09-25).

D11.behavior: Releasing a stroke journals one Add and stores the softness used. Width, softness, and foreground edits from keys or HUDs are tool state and are not journaled. Releasing the color wheel keeps the foreground and writes it into the 24-slot recent list. A brush stroke is a radial bitmap of its centerline (Stroke.stamp, and any softness above zero). Both painters share that bitmap: opaque out to (1 - softness) of the radius, clear at the rim, maximum coverage where dabs overlap. Coverage is dithered to 8 bits on a world-aligned grid, so a wide soft falloff does not band into rings and neighbouring tiles continue one pattern. The HTML artifact embeds the PNG. A hard non-brush stroke stays a vector path. A Shift segment that starts at the end of the last brush mark extends that stroke instead of adding a node, with one tip per vertex, so the chain is one stamp: joints and self-overlaps never exceed the opacity, and each segment is its own undo step. A size, color or opacity HUD opened mid-stroke pauses sampling, so the scrub paints nothing; the samples after it blend from the last drawn tip to the new one by smoothstep over 24 screen px (or the wider tip), the live stroke shows that blend, and the committed stroke keeps one stamped tip per vertex (P1.curve.tip-chord; user, 27 September 2026). Finished brush strokes use Photoshop's default Normal blend: source-over, opacity on the whole stroke, so one stroke does not build past that opacity and a later stroke covers an earlier one. Committing a stroke never blanks earlier strokes: each cached tile keeps painting its previous raster until the replacement lands, and tiles the new stroke does not touch keep their textures. Erasing never blanks strokes the eraser did not reach: while a pass lifts reached strokes out of the cache, the tiles from before the pass stand in for the rest until their own rasters land. No commit rasterizes a large stroke on the frame loop (user, 27 September 2026: "ran f4 erasor lock up interface on commit of comand"). A stroke bitmap over SYNC_STAMP_PX builds on the raster workers and the newest result wins. Until the exact bitmap lands, a stand-in paints: the live brush canvas after a brush release, the eraser preview after an erase release, or the stroke's previous bitmap mapped onto its current frame after a smooth, restyle, move, or zoom. After an erase release the un-erased stroke never paints again. While that live canvas still shows the stroke under the same camera, a Shift press that continues the stroke starts its preview from the canvas and re-stamps nothing on the frame loop, however long the chain has grown (tip18). The Shift segment itself stamps on the raster workers too, and the newest request wins: every move frame paints the segment's tipped vector mesh (from the end of the last exact stamp when the drag only lengthened it), the exact stamp replaces that mesh within a few frames of the pointer stopping, and the release keeps the exact stamp, so no move or release frame stamps the segment on the frame loop. Anything that changes the stroke or the camera (an undo, a zoom, moving the stroke) makes the next Shift press rebuild the canvas. In an image paint session a Shift segment from the last mark extends that layer mark the same way, one layer patch per segment. The Eraser's Shift pass never stamps on the frame loop either (2026-09-27): per reached stroke, the raster workers cut the segment out of that stroke's ink, one job at a time and newest first; until the cut for the current segment lands, every move frame paints the eraser's band in its preview color over the part not yet cut, and the release takes in the cut that shows the final segment (it stamps once on the frame loop only when that cut has not landed). The committed erase mark is unchanged. Textures follow the Textures section.

D12.behavior: Esc during SizeHud or the color wheel restores width, softness, and foreground from the moment the right button went down, then closes the overlay. Brush stays armed. The next Esc disarms to Select. A stroke still commits on pointer release.

D13.behavior: P1.shape.properties: a selected stroke keeps the shared Fill / Stroke / Corners strip; it shows no dimension stringers (D08).

D14.behavior: A committed stroke keeps the softness it was painted with. Recoloring that stroke later leaves the brush softness where it was. The temporary Alt eyedropper, and the Eyedropper tool, still sample across the desktop.

D15.behavior: The selection strip gains no size or softness control. This pass adds no opacity digits, flow, airbrush, or brush-preset cycling on comma/period. The color wheel has no Space-to-jump between hue and saturation.

D16.behavior: Deviates P1.curve.create-style: foreground, width, softness, and round caps stay on the brush. The stroke is a uniform radial stamp so it matches the round tip. A style edit on a selected shape does not change them. The stroke stores the softness that was current at release.

D17.behavior: SizeHud and the color wheel consume the pointer for the whole right-button hold, so they neither paint, select, nor open the context menu. Committed ink is still picked on its stroke width, including at 0 percent opacity.

shape-content.reference: User request, 2026-09-18; existing Slate Text, crop and dynamic panels

D01.behavior: Double-click anywhere on an unlocked closed shape (rectangle, ellipse, or closed path, including an unfilled interior) to open the text editing configuration and a blinking caret. The Text control stays on the selection palette while that session is open and whenever the shape's text is non-empty.

D02.behavior: P1.shape.properties: the property strip stays attached to selection. Text editing is a session on the existing shape, not a sticky drawing tool; finishing returns to ordinary Select.

D03.behavior: New shape text is center-justified (TextAlign::Center) and wraps inside an inset of the shape. The caret blinks at the insertion point of that centered block. Ellipses and closed paths use the same inset of their bounds and clip glyphs to the outline. Re-entry keeps the stored alignment.

D04.behavior: P1.node.select/move remain unchanged. A double-click enters typing; dragging selected text selects characters. Property controls own their pointer gestures and never start a shape move.

D05.behavior: Text fields own typing, clipboard and text-selection keys. Enter inserts a paragraph. Outside text editing, retain the existing selection, transform and Alt plain-drop behavior.

D06.behavior: P0.9: text, caret, palette, clipping and hit regions follow the host through zoom, pan and rotation. Host movement/resizing keeps P1.node.transform and snapping. Cache derived interior and clip geometry on change.

D07.behavior: No direction lock for typing. Proposed overflow rule: keep the authored shape and font size fixed, wrap inside the text area, and show an overflow indication while editing/selected; retain all text for editing. Never silently enlarge the shape or shrink the type.

D08.behavior: Typeface and text height are fillet capsules at CORNER_HEIGHT; the menu arrow sits in a circle at the capsule end. Typefaces are Sans, Serif, Mono, and the installed system faces in Typeface. Text height offers 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96 (default 24). Justification is Left, Center, or Right. Font color uses the shared color editor. Color, typeface, size, and justification update the caret immediately, and selection follows the aligned glyphs. One style applies to the whole block.

D09.behavior: P1.shape.properties selection fading applies while the Text adjustment panel is open. Typed characters paint in the shape as they are entered.

D10.behavior: A blinking insertion caret appears inside the text area, without a separate text window. Text hover uses the I-beam.

D11.behavior: P0.2/P0.3: a finished text session and each formatting change are invertible SceneCmd groups. Preserve the host id, geometry, stroke, transforms and links. Empty or unchanged sessions add no undo step.

D12.behavior: Match existing text behavior: Escape or click outside finishes and commits typing; Ctrl+Z undoes the session. Escape cancels an uncommitted Text-palette preview.

D13.behavior: Double-click opens the Text editor above the selection strip: typeface capsule, justification, text-height capsule, and color access. The Text squircle stays while editing and whenever the shape's text is non-empty. Follow DYNAMIC_PANELS.md and P1.shape.properties. No Apply/Cancel footer.

D14.behavior: Double-click the shape again to resume typing at the stored text. Clearing the text removes the Text control from the palette.

D15.behavior: One typeface, size, color, and justification for the whole shape text block. No mixed-font spans, bold, underline, text-on-path, linked text frames, or a new drawing tool. Shape image fill stays out of this pass.

D16.behavior: First text on a shape uses center alignment, Sans, size 24, and the Text tool's ink color. Re-entry keeps the shape's stored family, size, color, and alignment.

D17.behavior: Only unlocked closed regions accept text: rectangle, ellipse, and closed paths, including stars and concave trims. Open curves, holes, hidden nodes, and locked nodes do not enter text edit. An unfilled closed interior still accepts the double-click.

portal-slate-board.reference: Nested Slate workbook board (Art. V.3 document portal, spike S1)

D01.behavior: Slate board only. Command `board.portal.slate`. Palette name "slate board" (aliases: nested board, workbook portal). Portals flyout, no single-key chord. Not a File Atlas feature.

D02.behavior: P2.PortalPlace.oneshot / P0.4. One-shot: commit returns to Select. Space or Enter re-arms.

D03.behavior: P2.PortalPlace.gesture: Armed, then Dragging(rect), then Committed(unbound). Release paints "Choose workbook…". Binding is a separate step (D19).

D04.behavior: P2.PortalPlace.click. Travel under `draft.drag_threshold` (4 screen px) places 960×540 world units (`PORTAL_DEFAULT_W` × `PORTAL_DEFAULT_H`) centred on the click. Past the threshold, the drag is the rect.

D05.behavior: P2.PortalPlace.aspect. Shift during the drag locks 16:9. An unmodified drag is free-aspect. Ctrl and Alt do nothing during placement.

D06.behavior: P2.PortalPlace.snap. Grid snap and smart guides apply to the frame rect. The child scene does not snap to the parent grid. No ortho lock.

D07.behavior: n/a. Rect placement has no directional parameter.

D08.behavior: No digit entry during placement. After bind, Rebind edits the path. Frame size uses the existing node resize, not a new numeric mode.

D09.behavior: While dragging: portal outline and live width × height in the dock readout. Bound and idle: file name, health (Ok, Unknown, or Missing). Selected readout adds the relative locator and whether that workbook is an open tab.

D10.behavior: Crosshair while armed. Arrow over the frame, the maximize square, and the chrome. Version one has no contents-focus cursor.

D11.behavior: One journaled Add: rect, class Document, kind Slate, source None. Binding later is a Patch. The child scene is not copied into the parent journal. One gesture is one undo. No BoardLastStyle (D16).

D12.behavior: Esc during the drag cancels placement and returns to Select (P0.1). Esc on a selected portal does not unbind it. Maximize, if up, peels first (D34). There is no contents-focus layer in version one.

D13.behavior: P1.portal.pick and P1.node.transform. Hover resize, axis-aligned, no rotate chrome. P1.node.corner-grip on the portal frame. Child nodes are not grips. Maximize square per P1.portal.chrome.

D14.behavior: Rebind is `portal.slate.source`, a journaled Patch that drops the cached child. Resize refits the same child (D20). Edits to the board happen in the child tab and stay on the child journal.

D15.behavior: Cut in version one: in-place editing; contents-focus tools; the child's Grid, Venn, or Lens; a second Slate process; a WebView of the export; binding the parent path; a `.slate` drop on empty canvas becoming a portal; bake-merging the child into the parent; agent writes into the child; reading secrets. Not cut: place, bind a local `.slate`, fitted paint of the child's Board, open-in-tab, refresh, cycle refusal, export of the child rendered in the frame.

D16.behavior: P1.portal.style. No BoardLastStyle. Unauthored fill follows Palette::card, slightly lighter than the canvas in both light and dark. No outline unless portal.stroke is authored. Theme changes do not write the scene.

D17.behavior: P1.portal.pick. Click and marquee hit the frame rect. A click on the painted child selects the frame, not a child node. `border_hit_px` comes only from `portal_frame_tokens`.

D18.behavior: Document (Art. V.3). The child workbook's journal owns mutations of that board. The parent journals the frame only: rect, title, source, fill, stroke. `PortalClass::Document` is new. Determinism is not required.

D19.behavior: Dropping a `.slate` file on a board whose scene already has nodes opens a chooser: Open (the existing tab path, `open_doc_at`) or Insert (a bound Slate portal, 960×540, centred on the drop). A blank board, meaning no board nodes, skips the chooser and opens the file as a tab. Browse on an unbound Slate portal, or `portal.slate.source`, still binds. One `SourceUri`, a local `.slate` file, stored relative-first (Art. IX.2). Health is Ok, Missing, or Unknown, and the card names the locator. Refused: empty, a directory, a URL, a non-`.slate` file, the parent workbook path, and a locator that closes a cycle. Rebind is a journaled Patch. Child-internal links resolve against the child workbook.

D20.behavior: No journaled query in version one. The fitted region is the union of the child's visible Board node rects (see Fit). An empty union paints "Empty board". Frames are nodes in that union, not a paged deck.

D21.behavior: Load and reload run off the frame loop and are generation-tagged (Art. II.3). A stale load is dropped. Triggers: bind, `portal.slate.refresh`, and a changed child mtime. If that workbook is already an open tab, paint the live scene, including unsaved edits, instead of the disk copy. The last good scene stays up across a refresh.

D22.behavior: Click selects the frame. Double-click or Enter (`portal.slate.open`) opens the child through `open_doc_at`, which focuses the tab when that canonical path is already open. Wheel, pan, and board tools stay with the parent (P0.5). No contents-focus in version one. The fit inverse in Fit is the later edit-mode map.

D23.behavior: P0.9. Board zoom scales the portal and the fitted child together, with no screen-size floor. Type that is too small drops, using the board painter's existing LOD. The fit is in world space; screen size is that result times parent zoom.

D24.behavior: Document class: `slate-artifact` renders the child's Board into the frame with the same fit function (Art. IV). A caption names the relative locator and health. Unbound, Missing, cycle, and empty export that state card. Depth cap matches D29. The child secret store and WebView profile are not packaged. Portal frame fillet: portal_frame_corner; journal Corner::Square -> PORTAL_FRAME_DEFAULT_FILLET.

D25.behavior: No bake command in version one. Copying the child's nodes into the parent is a document merge and stays deferred. The portal remains a link.

D26.behavior: P1.portal.sync. Frame, source, fill, and stroke sync as journal deltas. Each peer resolves the relative locator and loads locally. A peer who cannot resolve it paints Unknown and names the locator. The loaded scene is not transmitted.

D27.behavior: `board.portal.slate`, `portal.slate.source`, `portal.slate.refresh`, and `portal.slate.open` are registry commands (Art. VII.1). Agent frame and source mutations stage for acceptance (Art. VII.6). An agent may not write the child, read secrets, or bind a cycle or the parent path. The beacon carries locator and health, not the child scene.

D28.behavior: Not deterministic (Art. V.3, document class). The caption is the relative locator, health, and the child mtime when known. Two peers may differ while one has unsaved tab edits (D21).

D29.behavior: One cached child scene per canonical path, shared by every portal on that file; the fit stays per portal. Generation tags drop stale loads. Paint depth is 2: a Slate portal inside the child paints the grandchild, and anything deeper paints a card naming the locator without loading it. The frame loop does not read the child file. Child tessellation is cached with the scene (Art. II).

D30.behavior: Unbound paints "Choose workbook…". Missing and Unknown name the locator. A wrong kind is refused and the frame stays unbound, with the reason. A cycle or a self-bind paints "This workbook already contains that board" and names both locators, without loading. An empty board paints "Empty board". An unreadable file paints the parse error. A failed child does not take down the parent board.

D31.behavior: Journaled: rect, title, source, fill, stroke. Derived, never journaled: loaded scene, fit transform, load generation, hover, maximize, open-tab hint. No inner camera in version one.

D32.behavior: Local `.slate` only. No network fetch, no script, no WebView. Loading parses the scene and does not start the child's agent sidecars, does not open the child's web portals as live pages, and does not read secrets. Child host portals paint their frame and empty or poster state inside the nest.

D33.behavior: P1.portal.chrome. No identity tab (web-only). Maximize square at the upper right. Right-click: Open workbook, Rebind, Refresh, Maximize. No Slate top bar inside the frame.

D34.behavior: P1.portal.maximize. Maximize fills the Slate canvas pane with the same fitted board, still read-only. The node rect is not mutated. Esc peels maximize first. Maximize does not open a tab.

D35.behavior: P1.portal.local-ui. Locator, health, Rebind, Refresh, and Open workbook stay on this portal's inspector and menu. They do not appear on Document Settings or any board-wide panel.

D01.behavior: Selecting one frame shows a Deck squircle on the selection strip, with the hover tooltip Order frames: click each one, or draw a stroke through them. It is not a tools-dock icon. No key. Command board.tool.deck, aliases slides and presentation order. Clicking the squircle arms the tool; clicking it again returns to Select. The squircle stays highlighted while armed. Repeat-last re-arms it.

D02.behavior: Sticky. A click or a finished stroke commits that order change and leaves the tool armed so the next frame or stroke can extend the same sequence. Another tool, or Esc with no stroke in progress, returns to Select.

D03.behavior: Armed. Click a frame to append it. Press and drag to draw a stroke; each frame whose rect the stroke first enters is appended in that order. Release commits the stroke. The stroke is preview only and is not a node.

D04.behavior: Pointer travel from press to release at or below draft.drag_threshold (4 screen px) is a click. Travel beyond that is a stroke. The split uses unsnapped screen travel, same as DragRect.

D05.behavior: No Shift, Ctrl, or Alt chord changes the gesture. Selection shortcuts do not run while the tool is armed.

D06.behavior: The stroke is freehand. F8 ortho, F9 grid, and object snaps do not move it. A frame counts when the stroke polyline first intersects its rect, topmost frame only where rects overlap.

D07.behavior: n/a. Tab does nothing. There is no length or angle to lock.

D08.behavior: n/a. Digits do not edit order. The existing frame Prev and Next squircles still swap neighbors after the tool is left.

D09.behavior: While armed, every frame shows its deck index (1-based position in frames_in_order) above the left end of its upper edge (the edge facing up on screen, so a rotated frame keeps the badge on top, like the frame title), through canvas_text at 14 world units, dropped when illegible (P0.9). The in-progress stroke paints in Palette::accent at width 2 world units. A frame lights as the stroke enters it. The dock readout shows n slides.

D10.behavior: Crosshair while armed, including over a frame.

D11.behavior: One journaled patch of FrameNode.order per click and per completed stroke, command board.tool.deck. A click appends a frame, or moves it to the end of the session if it is already there. A stroke appends only frames not yet in the session, in first-contact order. Untouched visible frames keep their previous relative order after that session. Hidden frames stay hidden and are not slides. A gesture that does not change order adds no undo step. One changed gesture is one undo. Re-arming keeps the session.

D12.behavior: Esc during a stroke drops the stroke and commits nothing. A second Esc disarms to Select. Committed order changes stay; Ctrl+Z undoes the last gesture.

D13.behavior: The tool does not select frames and does not show resize grips. Deck index badges are the only added chrome, and only while armed. Leaving the tool restores ordinary frame selection (P1.node.transform + P1.node.corner-grip on frames).

D14.behavior: Frame-strip Prev and Next still swap one selected frame with its neighbor. Re-arming Deck continues the same document order: further clicks and strokes append frames not yet in the session. Playback stays F5, View → Present, and the frame-strip Present squircle.

D15.behavior: Cut: a stored path or ink node; starting presentation on commit; hiding or deleting frames that were not touched; marquee select; changing fill, stroke, corner, or membership; reordering non-frames.

D16.behavior: The tool does not read or write BoardLastStyle. New frames stay on the frame recipe: fillet radius 8 (TEXT_CARD_FILLET) and no stroke. The Fill, Stroke, and Corners squircles still edit a selected frame.

D17.behavior: A click hits the topmost frame whose rect contains the point, the same rect test as Scene::frame_at. Empty board and non-frames do nothing. A stroke hits by polyline intersection with the frame rect, first contact wins, topmost on overlap.

select-sweep.reference: AutoCAD / Rhino window vs crossing marquee

D01.behavior: Existing Select tool: V, or the Select/Pan dock button. The sweep starts on left-drag on empty board, or on a frame body that selects its contents (frame_body_selects_contents). Command stays board.marquee. No new key.

D02.behavior: Select stays armed after release. The sweep does not change tool stickiness.

D03.behavior: Press, drag, release. Mode is the pointer's screen x against the press: pointer.x >= press.x is Window; pointer.x < press.x is Crossing. A drag with no horizontal travel is Window. The mode updates live while the button is held.

D04.behavior: A press on a pickable node still moves or scales it. A press on empty space, or a frame body, is the sweep. Release replaces or extends the selection even when the rect is only a few pixels; a miss on empty space clears the selection unless Shift or Ctrl is held.

D05.behavior: Shift or Ctrl held at release adds the hits to the current selection (P1.node.select). Neither modifier removes hits. Alt does not force Window. Pan chords (Space, middle, right) never start this sweep.

D06.behavior: The sweep rect is the raw screen drag converted by the camera. F8 ortho, F9 grid, and object snaps do not move its corners.

D07.behavior: n/a. Tab does not lock the sweep.

D08.behavior: n/a. Digits do nothing. Typing W or C during the drag does not force a mode.

D09.behavior: Window: solid 1 px stroke in palette.select and a fill of that color at alpha 0.12, which is today's preview. Crossing: dashed stroke, 6 px on and 4 px off, in a new token board.marquee.crossing (light #3D9A4A, dark #7DDEA0) with the same 0.12 fill. Both rects are screen-space chrome on the pointer drag, not canvas objects.

D10.behavior: The arrow cursor stays. No window or crossing glyph.

D11.behavior: Release writes board_sel. No modifier replaces it with the hits. Shift or Ctrl extends it. expand_board_selection still promotes a hit member to its group. The selection is not journaled. Hidden and locked nodes stay out. Frames are not selected. A sweep that started inside a frame only tests that frame's members.

D12.behavior: Esc during the drag drops the sweep and leaves board_sel unchanged.

D13.behavior: P1.node.transform after the selection lands. The sweep adds no grips of its own.

D14.behavior: n/a. The sweep does not create or edit geometry.

D15.behavior: Cut: Alt forcing Window; W/C typed aliases; Ctrl removing hits; File Atlas card marquee; the Z zoom-window; portal-internal file marquee; Direct Selection (A) anchor marquee, which keeps selecting anchors whose points lie inside the box.

D16.behavior: n/a. The sweep does not read or write BoardLastStyle.

D17.behavior: Window selects a node only when its pick geometry lies entirely inside the rect. Stroke-pick shapes and connectors: every flattened centerline sample is inside. Other nodes: all four corners of the rotated rect are inside. Crossing keeps marquee_hits_node: stroke intersection, or the rotated rect intersecting the sweep. A line that only crosses the box is selected right-to-left and missed left-to-right. A single-click brush dab is its ink disc (stroke width across): window needs the whole disc inside, crossing needs the rect to touch the disc, and a click anywhere on the disc picks it.

image-crop.reference: Image corner palette plus existing InDesign-style crop mode

D01.behavior: Crop lives in the Corners squircle, with the fillet. The panel shows Fillet/Chamfer and an Off/Crop control. Off/Crop is packed into the one Corners capsule, leading Fillet/Chamfer, the slider and %/u: the capsule and slider keep their sizes and the three toggle capsules scale by one factor to fit. Crop turns the mode on for every selected croppable image. C and double-click still enter that same mode. 3D, text cards, and workbooks stay ineligible.

D02.behavior: Crop stays on until Off is chosen in the Corners panel, Enter, Esc, or a tool other than Select. It is not a sticky drawing tool. A finished crop gesture joins repeat-last (P0.4): afterwards, a Space tap or Enter while idle re-enters crop mode on whatever image is selected then, however crop was first entered.

D03.behavior: All selected frames display the crop in real time with the prime. Each image shows a corner bracket and an edge bar on every side. Dragging one clips that side. The picture stays fixed in the world and the frame shrinks over it. Releasing writes that same crop onto every selected croppable image.

D04.behavior: A press that travels less than draft.drag_threshold (4 screen px) does not clip. The Off/Crop control is a click and never starts a board drag or a marquee.

D05.behavior: No extra modifier. Shift does not lock aspect. The multi-selection itself is what copies the crop. Alt-drag still duplicates nodes and does not start a crop.

D06.behavior: F8, F9, and object snap do not move a crop edge. The window stays inside the uncropped picture and cannot shrink below MIN_CROP_WORLD (8 world units) or 5% of the source on either axis.

D07.behavior: n/a. Tab does not lock a crop edge.

D08.behavior: n/a in this pass. There is no typed crop inset. The Corners capsule still edits the fillet.

D09.behavior: While crop is on, each selected croppable image shows the white brackets, edge bars, and a white crop border. The dimmed full picture and the scrim outside the window stay on the image under the pointer. The Corners squircle stays up, with Crop shown on. A press on a crop handle or on a cropping image is the crop gesture, not a click-away: the squircle stays up, the selection stays whole, and the very first press reaches the handle.

D10.behavior: Hit zones are screen-space and never smaller than HIT_SLOP_PX (8), like other board handles (canvas_scale::hit_px). A corner is a disc of radius CROP_ARM_PX + CROP_HIT_PAD_PX (16 at 1:1) around the corner point. An edge is a band of half-width CROP_BAR_THICK_PX / 2 + CROP_HIT_PAD_PX (6.5, floored to 8) along the whole side, not only the painted bar. Both reach outside the box. Hovering a zone shows its cursor: left and right use the horizontal resize cursor, top and bottom the vertical, corners the diagonals.

D11.behavior: Pointer-up writes one journal group: the grabbed image's new frame and Crop, and the same Crop on every other selected croppable image, each frame resized so its own picture stays put. An unchanged drag adds no undo step. Undo restores every image in that group. Every path that sends this image to an agent uses only the visible crop window. The hidden part of the source file is omitted.

D12.behavior: Esc during a drag restores the gesture-start frames and crops and leaves crop mode on. Esc or Enter with no drag exits crop mode and keeps the last committed crop. The Corners fillet is untouched.

D13.behavior: Crop on paints Photoshop crop chrome: a white corner bracket on each corner and a short white bar across the middle of each side, each with a dark edge. Ordinary resize handles hide on those images until crop turns off. The fillet stays in the same Corners squircle.

D14.behavior: Turning crop off leaves the authored Crop on the node. Turning it on again puts the brackets and bars on the current crop edges. Save and HTML export keep the existing crop serialization.

D15.behavior: No rule-of-thirds grid, no rotate-to-straighten, and no destructive pixel delete. Dragging inside the picture does not pan the photo.

D16.behavior: n/a. Crop does not read or write BoardLastStyle.

D17.behavior: Corners win over edges where their zones overlap. Across several selected images, a corner beats an edge, then the nearest handle wins. That hit overrides wires and other transient handles. Crop mode does not clear the rest of the selection: a click on a cropping image or inside a handle zone keeps crop mode and every selected image. Pressing empty canvas outside every zone exits crop mode and deselects, matching the selection strip.

smooth.reference: Rhino smoothing brush subset; brush HUD chords
inherits: P0.*, P1.node, P1.curve, P1.curve.pick, P2.StickyInk (arm only)

D01.behavior: S and board.tool.smooth arm Smoothing beside Brush and Eraser in the Shapes flyout ink group.

D02.behavior: Sticky like Brush/Eraser: stays armed after each pass; each drag is one undo group.

D03.behavior: Left-drag sweeps a circular brush over existing marks: every stroke the brush crosses along the drag is picked, and passes run every half radius so a fast drag leaves no gap. Shift+drag is a straight pass from the end of the last pass; the whole segment is recomputed from the scene as the pointer moves. No paint on empty canvas.

image-paint-layers.reference: Trace paper on placed raster images

D01.behavior: Layers are not filters. With an image selected, activating a hosting drawing tool (including Eraser) starts painting on it; the first stroke creates a layer when the image has none, in the same undo step. While painting, the layer palette hangs centered below the image for the whole session; its small circled + just outside the right end appends a layer, makes it active, and keeps the tool armed. A click on a layer circle makes that layer active. The photo-filter capsule holds filters only. Agent and generator pictures are eligible whenever they show a raster result, picked or not (until one is picked, the newest), and their selection strip offers the photo-filter squircle before the Agent squircle.

D02.behavior: Drawing tools keep their stickiness. Image hosting ends on empty-canvas click or Esc after HUD peel.

D03.behavior: Hosted strokes use the armed tool grammar; commits outside the visible image outline are dropped.

D04.behavior: Existing per-tool click vs drag thresholds; layer circles, color dots, and + are click-only. A press anywhere on the layer palette never starts a stroke.

D05.behavior: Hosted tools keep their modifier maps; no layer-specific modifiers.

D06.behavior: Snap applies in world space; points outside the visible crop window do not commit.

D07.behavior: Inherited from hosted tool; no layer Tab locks.

D08.behavior: The layer palette's slider sets the active layer's opacity (0-100%); a click on its thumb types a value. The thumb follows the drag and release commits one journaled board.image.layer.opacity step (one undo); the image re-composites on release, not per frame, because the composite is a rasterized SVG (Art. II). Filter intensity stays on the filter capsule's own track.

D09.behavior: Each layer circle previews that layer's ink alone, center-cropped, rebuilt once per scene generation; a layer without a preview shows its index. Painting suppresses the selection's blue cast, dimension stringers, and fillet grip. Ink previews clip to crop, rotation, and fillet. Up to six document recent colors sit inside the layer palette as small dots between the layer circles and the slider; click sets brush/tool color via ViewState.recent_colors. On agent/generator pictures, suppress prompt readout, chips, verb pill, and album strip while hosting; they return when the session ends.

D10.behavior: Hosted tool cursors unchanged by clipping.

D11.behavior: Layers and opacity patch ImageNode; strokes are child nodes in normalized host space; Eraser affects active layer strokes only; filters affect base image only; layers composite above. Wired generator inputs use a derived PNG composite (filtered base + visible layers) written under slate-composite at send time.

D12.behavior: Esc exits hosting; strip previews discard like other shape properties.

D13.behavior: Layer palette: a dark rounded capsule at the filter height, centered 10 units below the image's rotated bounds, canvas-scaled. Left to right: layer circles (filter-radio size; only the active one carries the accent ring), recent-color dots, and the opacity slider (120-unit track as thick as a circle's radius); the circled + sits 6 units past the right end on its vertical center. Shown only while a hosting tool paints the sole selected image; the whole palette is editor chrome. The filter capsule holds filters only.

D14.behavior: Image transform carries layer geometry; replace-base-image keeps adjust, crop, and paint_layers. Image-on-image move and an external raster file drop onto an image show fixed Replace and Add as layer capsules beside the target. The dragged image is never its own target: the target is the topmost image under the pointer other than the one being dragged. The offer holds while the pointer crosses from the target to the capsule row. A file-drop offer ends only on Esc or real pointer movement away from both target and row; the pointer position egui kept from before the OS drag does not dismiss it. The capsules are a foreground widget: a press on one is that choice even if it drifts, and never drags the image beneath. Release on a capsule (move) or click on it (file drop) commits one command group; release elsewhere does nothing.

D15.behavior: Video/3D/text-card paint layers and layer reorder UI remain out of scope.

D16.behavior: Hosted strokes use active tool state, not unrelated BoardLastStyle.

D17.behavior: Pick layer ink only inside clipped outline; Eraser affects the active layer only; Delete while painting removes the active layer via board.image.layer.delete.
